content: We find that 1) a significant fraction of words that occur in everyday speech can be turned into McGurk-style illusions, 2) such illusions persist when embedded within the context of natural sentences, and in fact affect a significant fraction of natural sentences, and 3) the illusionability of words and sentences can be predicted using features from natural language modeling.
